scope: Observed local tokenizer-only diagnostic, transcribed from successful tool output. No model weights loaded, no NER predictions, no gold edits.

runtime.network_guard: Python socket.connect, socket.create_connection and socket.getaddrinfo denied before tokenizer imports. Not an OS sandbox.

text:
父亲：
周明拿起 Nike 外套。

comparisons.example: Transformer word 4 (周 at chars 4:5) is written to embedding word index 3; original splitter index 3 maps to newline chars 3:4.

comparisons.filter: Retain tuple only if not token_text.isspace(); do not normalize text or change token start/end offsets.

source_locations.mechanism: SpaCyTokenSplitter emits every token, including standalone whitespace.
prepare_word_mask counts observed distinct word IDs with seen_words instead of preserving numeric gaps.
prepare_inputs retains start/end arrays for all splitter tokens.
Predicted word span indexes map through the original splitter start/end arrays.

conclusion: A standalone newline is emitted at splitter index 3 but receives no transformer subtoken. Observed-word numbering then shifts left while original character maps retain the newline. Filtering pure-whitespace splitter tokens and retaining original non-whitespace offsets removes this demonstrated mismatch.
limitations: Tokenizer/aggregation mechanism only; no claim of improved NER accuracy until original 18 gold cases and actual prompt are rerun.
Other zero-subtoken Unicode tokens and normalization behaviours are not exhaustively covered.
Installed spacy.blank(zh) emits individual Latin letters, as shown by Nike tokenization.
Tokenizer conversion warned about missing fast-tokenizer byte fallback and a Mistral regex warning; these warnings are not established causes of the demonstrated newline index compression.
